title: Discussion: Roommates sharing a warehouse store membership
context: You will hear four roommates in Vancouver discussing whether to buy household items together at a bulk warehouse store.

segments.speaker: Sofia
segments.text: Okay, house meeting. I added up everyone's grocery receipts for October, and between the four of us we spent just over fourteen hundred dollars. A lot of that is the same stuff bought four times. Four jugs of olive oil, four bags of rice, four different brands of dish soap.

segments.speaker: Kwame
segments.text: Guilty on the dish soap, Sofia. But in my defence, nobody labels anything, so I never know what's mine.

segments.speaker: Anjali
segments.text: That's kind of the point, though, isn't it? If we shared the basics, we wouldn't need labels. I've been thinking we should get a BulkWay membership. It's sixty-five dollars a year, and toilet paper alone is something like a third cheaper there.

segments.speaker: Ethan
segments.text: I'm all for saving money, but where are we going to put it all? Our pantry is one shelf above the fridge. If we bring home a forty-eight pack of paper towels, it ends up living in my room, and I'm not okay with that.

segments.speaker: Anjali
segments.text: We could use the hall closet. It's full of Kwame's bike gear right now.

segments.speaker: Kwame
segments.text: Hey, my bike gear has to go somewhere. But fine, I can hang the bike up in the storage locker downstairs if someone helps me put up a hook.

segments.speaker: Sofia
segments.text: Can I raise the real issue? It's not storage, it's fairness. I eat a lot of rice and beans, and Ethan basically lives on protein shakes and chicken. If we split everything equally, someone's going to end up paying for someone else's dinner.

segments.speaker: Ethan
segments.text: To be fair, I'd be paying for your rice too.

segments.speaker: Sofia
segments.text: Rice is two dollars a kilo, Ethan. Your chicken isn't.

segments.speaker: Anjali
segments.text: So we don't share actual food. We share the things everyone goes through at about the same rate: cleaning supplies, toilet paper, cooking oil, coffee, maybe spices. Everything else stays personal.

segments.speaker: Kwame
segments.text: Coffee's a stretch. I have one cup a day, and Sofia goes through a whole pot before noon.

segments.speaker: Sofia
segments.text: Okay, that's fair. Coffee goes on the personal list.

segments.speaker: Ethan
segments.text: And how do we actually split the bill, Anjali? I don't want to be chasing people for eleven dollars every week.

segments.speaker: Anjali
segments.text: There's an app called SplitPot. Whoever pays uploads the receipt, and it keeps a running balance. We settle up once a month.

segments.speaker: Kwame
segments.text: Who's driving, though? Only Ethan has a car, and BulkWay is out in Burnaby.

segments.speaker: Ethan
segments.text: I don't mind driving once a month, but then my gas should count as a shared cost too. It's twenty-five minutes each way.

segments.speaker: Sofia
segments.text: That seems more than reasonable. Okay, so: one membership, shared household stuff only, a monthly trip with Ethan driving, and gas goes into the app.

segments.speaker: Anjali
segments.text: The membership will be in my name, but I can add one extra cardholder for free, so let's add Ethan, since he's the one going.

segments.speaker: Kwame
segments.text: Great. I'll clear out the closet this weekend. Someone just remind me to buy that hook.

questions.prompt: What problem does Sofia point out at the beginning?

options.text: Each roommate spent more than $1,400 in October.
options.whyVi: 1.400 đô là tổng của cả bốn người, không phải mỗi người.

options.text: Someone has been using other people's dish soap.
options.whyVi: Bài có 'dish soap', nhưng vấn đề là mỗi người mua riêng một chai, không phải dùng trộm.

options.text: The pantry is too small for all their groceries.
options.whyVi: Ethan mới là người nói tủ đồ quá nhỏ, và nói sau đó.

options.text: They keep buying the same products separately.
options.whyVi: Đúng: cùng một món được mua bốn lần (dầu ô liu, gạo, nước rửa chén).

questions.evidence: A lot of that is the same stuff bought four times.
questions.explanationVi: 'The same stuff bought four times' được diễn đạt lại thành 'buying the same products separately'.

questions.prompt: How does Ethan feel about buying in bulk at first?

options.text: He thinks the membership is too expensive.
options.whyVi: Ethan không phàn nàn về giá 65 đô.

options.text: He likes saving money but does not want bulk items stored in his room.
options.whyVi: Đúng: anh ủng hộ tiết kiệm nhưng không chấp nhận đồ để trong phòng mình.

options.text: He refuses to share anything with his roommates.
options.whyVi: Sai: anh nói 'I'm all for saving money' và cuối cùng còn nhận lái xe.

options.text: He worries that the store is too far away.
options.whyVi: Kwame là người nhắc BulkWay ở tận Burnaby.

questions.evidence: it ends up living in my room, and I'm not okay with that
questions.explanationVi: 'I'm all for saving money, but...' cho thấy đồng ý về nguyên tắc nhưng có điều kiện. Mối lo thực sự của anh là chỗ để đồ.

questions.prompt: What does Kwame agree to do to make space?

options.text: Move his bike into a storage area in the building
options.whyVi: Đúng: anh sẽ treo xe đạp trong kho chứa đồ ở tầng dưới.

options.text: Sell some of his bike gear
options.whyVi: Kwame không nói sẽ bán đồ.

options.text: Keep the paper towels in his own room
options.whyVi: Chuyện khăn giấy trong phòng là của Ethan, và anh không đồng ý.

options.text: Build shelves inside the hall closet
options.whyVi: Bài có 'put up a hook' (gắn móc) chứ không phải đóng kệ trong tủ.

questions.evidence: I can hang the bike up in the storage locker downstairs
questions.explanationVi: 'The storage locker downstairs' được diễn đạt lại thành 'a storage area in the building'.

options.text: Ethan should eat healthier food.
options.whyVi: Cô không bình luận về sức khỏe.

options.text: Rice should be bought in bulk to save money.
options.whyVi: Cô nhắc 'rice' để so sánh giá, không đề nghị mua gạo số lượng lớn.

options.text: Splitting all costs equally would be unfair because they eat differently.
options.whyVi: Đúng: mỗi người ăn khác nhau nên chia đều sẽ có người trả tiền bữa tối cho người khác.

options.text: Storage is the biggest problem for the group.
options.whyVi: Ngược lại: cô nói 'It's not storage, it's fairness'.

questions.explanationVi: Sofia chuyển trọng tâm ('Can I raise the real issue?'): vấn đề là công bằng. Lý do: cô ăn gạo và đậu rẻ, Ethan ăn gà và sữa protein đắt hơn.

questions.prompt: When Kwame says "Coffee's a stretch", what does he mean?

options.text: Coffee takes too long to make every morning.
options.whyVi: Không ai nói pha cà phê mất thời gian.

options.text: Including coffee in the shared items goes too far.
options.whyVi: Đúng: 'a stretch' = hơi quá, khó chấp nhận, vì mỗi người uống lượng rất khác nhau.

options.text: Coffee is something everyone uses equally.
options.whyVi: Ngược lại: anh uống một ly, Sofia uống cả bình.

options.text: Coffee is too expensive at BulkWay.
options.whyVi: Anh không nói về giá cà phê ở cửa hàng.

questions.evidence: Coffee's a stretch. I have one cup a day, and Sofia goes through a whole pot before noon.
questions.explanationVi: 'That's a stretch' = điều đó hơi quá, khó coi là hợp lý. Anh giải thích ngay sau: lượng dùng của mỗi người chênh nhau quá nhiều.

questions.prompt: Which items will the roommates share in the end?

options.text: Coffee and spices
options.whyVi: Gia vị có thể chia chung, nhưng cà phê đã bị chuyển sang danh sách riêng.

options.text: Chicken and rice
options.whyVi: Đồ ăn thật sự được giữ riêng ('we don't share actual food').

options.text: Protein shakes and toilet paper
options.whyVi: Giấy vệ sinh thì chung, nhưng sữa protein là đồ ăn riêng của Ethan.

options.text: Toilet paper and products for cleaning
options.whyVi: Đúng: giấy vệ sinh và đồ dùng lau dọn nằm trong danh sách đồ chung.

questions.evidence: We share the things everyone goes through at about the same rate: cleaning supplies, toilet paper, cooking oil, coffee, maybe spices.
questions.explanationVi: Danh sách ban đầu có cà phê, nhưng sau đó Sofia đồng ý 'Coffee goes on the personal list'. Cần nghe đến cuối để loại bỏ cà phê. 'Cleaning supplies' được diễn đạt lại thành 'products for cleaning'.

questions.prompt: Why will Ethan be added to the membership?

options.text: He will be the one doing the shopping trips.
options.whyVi: Đúng: Anjali thêm Ethan vì anh là người lái xe đi mua.

options.text: He will pay the yearly fee.
options.whyVi: Không ai nói Ethan trả phí thành viên; thẻ đứng tên Anjali.

options.text: The card must be in the driver's name.
options.whyVi: Thẻ chính đứng tên Anjali, không phải người lái xe.

options.text: He uses the most shared household items.
options.whyVi: Không ai nói Ethan dùng đồ chung nhiều nhất.

questions.evidence: let's add Ethan, since he's the one going
questions.explanationVi: 'Since he's the one going' (vì anh là người đi) được diễn đạt lại thành 'doing the shopping trips'. Cần nhớ trước đó Ethan nhận lái xe mỗi tháng.

questions.prompt: What does Ethan ask for in return for driving?

options.text: He wants someone else to drive every second month.
options.whyVi: Anh nói 'I don't mind driving once a month', không yêu cầu thay phiên.

options.text: He wants to be paid for his time.
options.whyVi: Anh chỉ muốn chia tiền xăng, không đòi trả công cho thời gian.

options.text: He wants his fuel costs to be shared by everyone.
options.whyVi: Đúng: tiền xăng phải được tính là chi phí chung.

options.text: He wants to skip paying for the membership.
options.whyVi: Anh không nhắc đến phí thành viên.

questions.evidence: my gas should count as a shared cost too
questions.explanationVi: 'My gas should count as a shared cost' được diễn đạt lại thành 'fuel costs to be shared by everyone'. Sau đó Sofia tóm tắt: 'gas goes into the app'.

review.notes: Solved all 8 items independently; keys match, one defensible answer each (Q6 correctly requires noticing coffee was moved to the personal list). Added name cues for Sofia and Anjali (Anjali was never named). Lowered difficulty 8 -> 7: answers are mostly explicit with light paraphrase and two idioms.
